meta.title: Check your understanding: Current, voltage and power

objectives: Identify the short-circuit current, open-circuit voltage and maximum power point on an I-V curve
Calculate fill factor and efficiency from a cell's measured values
Predict how light, temperature and resistance change the I-V curve

questions.prompt: Thin cloud halves the light on the lab cell, from 1000 to 500 W/m². What happens to its short-circuit current (I_sc) and open-circuit voltage (V_oc)?
choices: I_sc halves, but V_oc falls by only about 18 mV
V_oc halves, but I_sc stays the same
I_sc halves, and V_oc rises slightly to make up for it
questions.explain: I_sc is set by how many photons make pairs, so it follows the light. V_oc depends on the logarithm of the light current, so halving the light costs only kT/q × ln 2 ≈ 18 mV. That is why cells still give a useful voltage on cloudy days.

questions.prompt: At 500 W/m² the 243 cm² lab cell gives I_sc = 4.86 A, V_oc = 0.686 V and P_max = 2.75 W. What is its efficiency?
questions.explain: Efficiency is P_max ÷ (G × A) = 2.75 ÷ (500 × 0.0243) ≈ 22.6 %, almost the same as at full sun. Dividing by 1000 W/m² gives 11 %, but the cell only received 500 W/m². Using V_oc × I_sc (3.33 W) gives 27 %, a power the cell never delivers.

questions.prompt: On a hot roof the lab cell warms from 25 °C to 50 °C under the same light. What happens?
choices: V_oc falls by about 2 mV per degree, the current rises slightly, and power falls
Power rises, because hot silicon absorbs more of the red end of the spectrum
The current falls sharply while the voltage stays the same
Nothing changes, because the efficiency is rated at standard test conditions
questions.explain: Heat makes the junction leak much more, so the voltage falls, from 0.704 V to 0.656 V in the lab. The current does rise a little because hot silicon absorbs slightly more red light, but far less than the voltage falls, so the power drops by about 0.3 % per °C.

questions.prompt: In the I-V lab you raise the series resistance from 0.5 to 3 Ω·cm². What do you see?
choices: V_oc drops sharply, while the fill factor stays the same
I_sc drops to about half, and the flat top of the curve tilts
The fill factor and maximum power fall, while V_oc stays the same
The knee becomes sharper and the maximum power rises
questions.explain: Series resistance eats voltage in proportion to the current, so it tilts the steep right-hand side and drags the knee down: the fill factor falls from 0.82 to 0.69 and P_max from 5.60 to 4.73 W. At open circuit no current flows, so V_oc does not change. A tilted flat top is the sign of a low shunt resistance instead.
